Action Plan:
1. Provide first-line analgesia for acute unilateral headache: advise patient to start ibuprofen (high-dose migraine regimen; exact dose/route/frequency not documented) and may continue paracetamol as needed.
2. Recommend one week of self-certified sick leave from work to reduce suspected stress-related triggers.
3. Supply self-referral link for local counselling/CBT service to address ongoing anxiety and work stress.
4. Counsel on lifestyle triggers: aim for 7–8 h sleep nightly; maintain 1.5–2 L non-caffeinated fluids daily; monitor caffeine intake.
5. Issue written “headache red-flag” information sheet and advise low threshold for re-contacting GP/urgent care if red-flag symptoms develop or pain worsens.
6. Arrange routine follow-up consultation in 1 week to review response; consider blood tests or further work-up if no improvement.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden severe left-sided headache awakening patient at ~05:30 today.  
• History of presenting illness:  
  – Onset: this morning; woke patient from sleep.  
  – Character: constant, unilateral (left) pain; worst headache experienced to date.  
  – Associated symptoms: mild photophobia; brief morning dizziness (resolved); no nausea/vomiting; no neck stiffness; no fever; pain somewhat eases after lying down.  
  – Exacerbating/relieving: paracetamol ineffective; rest mild relief.  
• Previous headaches: intermittent, less-severe frontal “cluster/band-like” headaches; never strictly unilateral before.  
• Past medical history: Generalised anxiety disorder (≈2 yrs). No hypertension or other chronic disease.  
• Medications: Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented); single dose paracetamol today.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Social history: Lives with partner; non-smoker; runs 3×/week; average diet; owns a cat; significant work stress/late nights ×2 months.  
• Family history: Mother with anxiety; no migraine or major medical conditions reported.

Objective:
• Telephone/video consultation – no vitals or physical examination possible.  
• Patient reports no focal neurologic deficits.  
• No investigations performed during call.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute severe unilateral headache  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Migraine without aura (DDx: High) versus tension-type headache (DDx: Medium).  
   – Differential diagnosis:  
     • Migraine without aura – High (consistent unilateral pain, photophobia, stress/sleep deprivation trigger).  
     • Tension-type headache – Medium (work stress, prior milder bilateral headaches).  
     • Cluster headache – Low-Medium (early-morning unilateral pain; lacks autonomic features).  
     • Subarachnoid haemorrhage – Low but serious (sudden severe pain waking patient).  
     • Intracranial mass – Low (new unilateral morning pain; single-day history).  
   – Investigations planned: None immediately; consider blood tests ± neuro-imaging if no improvement or red-flag symptoms develop.  
   – Treatment: Start ibuprofen (high-dose migraine regimen, dose/route/frequency not documented); may continue paracetamol; advise hydration and rest.  
   – Referrals: None at present; urgent referral to ED if red-flag features occur.

2. Work-related stress / Generalised anxiety disorder  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Ongoing generalized anxiety disorder, currently exacerbated by workload.  
   – Differential diagnosis: Adjustment reaction to work stress.  
   – Investigations planned: None.  
   – Treatment: One week self-certified leave; maintain sertraline; lifestyle advice (sleep, exercise).  
   – Referrals: Provide counselling/CBT self-referral link.

3. Lifestyle optimisation (sleep hygiene & hydration)  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Contributing lifestyle factors to headache.  
   – Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.  
   – Investigations planned: None.  
   – Treatment: Encourage 7–8 h sleep nightly, 1.5–2 L water/day, reduce caffeine, regular exercise.  
   – Referrals: None.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: No vitals or neurological examination possible via phone; exact ibuprofen dose not documented; sertraline dose not recorded; alcohol intake not discussed; no BP measurement.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; no notable omissions or inaudible segments.
